text.en: In the lab Raju saw a preserved leech and a rabbit model. "Their bodies show how organ systems work," said his teacher.

The Indian cattle leech lives in freshwater and sucks blood. The chapter studies its external form, the divisions of its body and the body wall, how it moves with suckers, and its digestive, respiratory, circulatory, excretory, nervous and reproductive systems.
The rabbit is a mammal with a body cavity, the coelom. It has a digestive system suited to eating plants, a respiratory system with lungs, a circulatory system with a four-chambered heart, an excretory system with kidneys, a nervous system and a reproductive system.
Comparing the two animals shows how structure fits the way of life, and how organ systems work together in an animal's body.
The Indian cattle leech lives in freshwater and sucks blood.

The chapter studies its external form, the divisions of its body and the body wall, how it moves with suckers, and its digestive, respiratory, circulatory, excretory, nervous and reproductive systems.
The rabbit is a mammal with a body cavity, the coelom.

It has a digestive system suited to eating plants, a respiratory system with lungs, a circulatory system with a four-chambered heart, an excretory system with kidneys, a nervous system and a reproductive system.
Comparing the two animals shows how structure fits the way of life, and how organ systems work together in an animal's body.
The Indian cattle leech is an annelid. Its long body is organised in a series of segments, giving it a different arrangement from a rabbit.
The textbook’s body map groups thirty-three segments of the cattle leech. The fine rings visible on its surface are not a reliable way to count the main segments.
The anterior sucker is at the front around the mouth. The larger posterior sucker is at the rear.
A sucker can attach while muscles move another part of the body. The front sucker also helps the leech feed.
For a loop-like move, the leech anchors its posterior sucker and extends the front of the body.
The anterior sucker then holds while the posterior sucker releases. The body shortens and brings the rear attachment forward.
In water, body movements can travel along the leech in waves. The waves help the animal move without alternate attachment to a surface.
Food passes into a digestive tract. The crop is a storage region, so a meal can remain there before it moves farther through the system.
A leech has no lungs. Oxygen moves across its moist body surface, and carbon dioxide moves out the other way.
The leech has channels running along the body. Pulsing side channels help move fluid and distribute substances.
Small organs called nephridia remove wastes from body fluids. Their openings reach the outside of the body.
Clusters of nerve cells are called ganglia. In the leech, ganglia linked along the ventral nerve cord help coordinate movement.

board.text: Ganglia relay signals along the body

text.en: The two sets of reproductive organs are present in one leech. This arrangement is called hermaphroditism.

board.text: One leech has both sets of organs

text.en: A rabbit has fur, visible outer ears and long hind legs. The powerful hind limbs help it hop.

board.text: Rabbit features: fur, ears and hind legs

text.en: Sharp front teeth cut food, and back teeth grind it. These tasks suit the rabbit’s plant-based diet.
The caecum is a pouch near the junction of the small and large intestines. Microbes there help break down parts of plant food.

board.text: The caecum helps process plant food

text.en: The diaphragm is a muscular sheet between the chest and abdominal cavities. The heart and lungs are in the chest.
Air goes through the windpipe, then through two main branches leading to the lungs. Smaller branches take it deeper inside.
When the diaphragm contracts it flattens, increasing chest space. Air can then flow into the expanding lungs.
The rabbit’s heart has two receiving chambers and two pumping chambers. The right side sends blood to the lungs, and the left side sends it to the body.
Blood goes between the heart and lungs to exchange gases. The other loop carries blood between the heart and the rest of the body.
Kidneys filter blood and remove waste such as urea. Urine passes from each kidney along a ureter to the bladder.
Sensory nerves carry signals from the body towards the brain and spinal cord. Other nerves help send commands to muscles.
Male and female rabbits have different reproductive organs. The young develop inside the mother before birth.
Both animals must get oxygen and remove wastes. A leech exchanges gases through its skin and has nephridia. A rabbit has lungs and kidneys.

problem.en: Which animal in this chapter is a mammal?

text.en: Mammals have hair and feed milk to young.
The rabbit has these features.
So the rabbit.

problem.en: A leech’s rear end is attached while its front stretches forward. What must happen next for a loop-like move?

text.en: The front sucker holds the new position.

why.en: The body needs an anchor before the rear end releases.

text.en: The rear sucker lets go and moves forward as the body shortens.

why.en: Alternating the two anchors produces forward movement.

problem.en: Explain how the rabbit’s heart and lungs work together to provide oxygen to a hind leg.

text.en: The right side of the heart sends blood to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen.

why.en: The lungs provide the gas exchange surface.

text.en: The blood returns to the left side of the heart and is pumped to the leg.

why.en: Blood vessels carry oxygen to the leg muscles.

problem.en: Compare the structures that remove wastes in a leech and in a rabbit.

text.en: A leech removes wastes through nephridia along the body.

why.en: Several repeated segments have these excretory structures.

text.en: A rabbit uses kidneys and sends urine to its bladder.

why.en: The organs differ, but both systems remove waste from the body.

prompt.en: A friend says The leech is a mammal. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: The leech is an annelid worm.

points.en: The leech is a blood-sucking annelid.
The rabbit is a mammal with a coelom.
